articles.title: De la euforia al vértigo: España se juega ante Japón su futuro en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Obligada a ganar para asegurar su pase (17.50 h TDP). Si vence y Alemania derrota a Mali, a cuartos • Si es segunda o tercera, a octavos • Y si es cuarta, a casa salvo triunfo africano
articles.summary: Obligada a ganar para asegurar su pase (17.50 h TDP). Si vence y Alemania derrota a Mali, a cuartos • Si es segunda o tercera, a octavos • Y si es cuarta, a casa salvo triunfo africano
articles.body: La inesperada, por sorprendente, derrota de España (7ª en el ranking FIBA) ante Mali (18ª), a la que siete días antes había aplastado por 39 puntos en un amistoso (97-58), la ha colocado de la noche a la mañana en el disparadero del Mundial. De confirmar su candidatura a las medallas tras arrollar en la primera jornada a la anfitriona Alemania (83-53), al batacazo ante el combinado africano (82-73) que la deja al borde del precipicio. Todo puede pasar a falta de la última jornada que se disputará este lunes en el Max-Schmeling-Halle (Berlín) con los dos partidos del grupo A a las 17.50 h: España-Japón y Mali-Alemania. Con los cuatro equipos igualados con una victoria y una derrota, todos pueden ocupar cualquier posición en función de los resultados que se den. Los tres primeros se clasificarán para los cruces: el líder, directamente a cuartos de final; el segundo y el tercero, a un cruce previo de octavos. Ese es el monumental lío en el que se ha metido España, un país de excesos en el que lo que un día es sublime al siguiente puede tornarse en catastrófico. Pero esta selección ni era el nuevo 'Dream Team' del baloncesto femenino tras la primera jornada ni es un desecho de tienta después de la segunda. Aunque algunos aventuraban, embriagados por la euforia de su estelar debut, que era la principal rival de Estados Unidos por el oro. Como si las potentísimas Francia y Australia no jugasen. Dentro de lo preocupante de esta situación tan incierta, lo más razonable es ver el vaso medio lleno, porque España depende de sí misma para clasificarse. Si gana a Japón se meterá en los cruces como primera o segunda, dependiendo del resultado del Alemania-Mali. Y si es como segunda, evitaría a Estados Unidos en una hipotética semifinal. E incluso en caso de derrota ante los nipones en el peor de los supuestos, podría acceder a octavos de final como tercera si las africanas derrotan a las anfitrionas. Lo más lógico, sin que eso signifique lanzar las campanas al vuelo, es que España se imponga a Japón, aunque el deporte es un territorio abonado para las sorpresas, como se vio ante Mali, donde lo previsible no siempre sucede y la coherencia puede mutar en incongruencia tras el salto inicial. Pero el sentido común, el juego colectivo, la experiencia, las estadísticas y los argumentos baloncestísticos de uno y otro dictan que España sobre el papel es mejor equipo que Japón. Y eso que la selección nipona, décima del ranking FIBA, no es ni mucho menos una perita en dulce. Quien así lo piense se equivoca y para darse cuenta de su error no tendría más que visionar -como ya hizo ayer la selección española- un resumen del partido que firmaron en su estreno mundialista para superar a Mali (102-97). Fue un partido en el que Japón batió el récord de triples en el campeonato con 20/35 (57,1%) y su jugadora Saki Hayashi el de triples en un partido del torneo con 9/15 (60%). España está avisada de dónde puede llegar el peligro de la selección asiática. Tomó buena nota de ello Alemania, que en la segunda jornada viendo el aluvión de triples nipón contra Mali, ató en corto a las tiradoras japonesas, de gatillo fácil, rebajando su porcentaje de triples a 3/27 (11%) anulando así su principal amenaza. Y fueron presa fácil para las germanas, que impusieron su mayor solidez y su físico (74-58). Alemania enseñó el camino del triunfo a España, que necesita recuperar su mejor versión tanto en lo colectivo como en lo individual para salir airosa de esta situación tan peliaguda en la que se ha metido. Urge que las de Miguel Méndez recuperen su confianza tras el palo ante Mali para volver a ser el equipo reconocible, competitivo, potente y fiable que es y no pareció ante las africanas. Si muestra su mejor cara, la que exhibió en su debut ante Alemania, España no tendrá problemas para tumbar a Japón. Pero si vuelve a sembrar las dudas, ya sea por cansancio, por falta de acierto exterior, o por dar medio metro de más a las peligrosísimas tiradoras niponas, podría pasar más apuros de los que desearía.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Unexpected Exchange With Italy Coach Goes Viral During Team USA Clash
articles.summary: The Caitlin Clark and Italy coach exchange had fans calling it ‘absolute comedy.’
articles.body:
Almost every WNBA fan waits for Caitlin Clark's sideline moments. Similarly, her recent exchange with Italy women's basketball head coach Andrea Capobianco caught the attention of eagle-eyed social media fans.

In their FIBA World Cup encounter on September 6, 2026, Team USA led Italy 13-8 with 2:03 remaining in the first quarter. But as two officials were debating a foul, the game came to a halt. When it came to speaking with a referee, Clark, who is often in the forefront of similar situations, got in on the action. Capobianco gave Clark one of his most animated reactions to date when he saw her. Now his reaction is making the rounds online.

The Mirror US reported that Capobianco said, "Non capisci, I seen you," fusing Italian and English when he addressed Clark , according to expert lip reader Nicola Hickling of LipReader Ltd. via Covers . According to Hickling, Clark's response was far more direct: "Stop complaining."

Either way, the online community had already started having a field day while watching the match live, as one X (formerly Twitter) user posted, "Caitlin rizzing the Italy coach 😭😭😭."

Another person joked, "He's confronting the wrong person 😂 Caitlin will argue with you."

Although Capobianco appeared to disagree with Clark on that particular point, the Italian head coach is wise enough not to ignore the brilliance of the Indiana Fever guard completely. This is because before Team USA's game against Italy, Capobianco had some kind words for Clark.

In a clip shared by Euro Women's Hoops on X, the Italian coach can be heard saying, "From a technical standpoint, I think Caitlin is incredible. From an image standpoint, she makes this sport even more enjoyable. Because, besides her ability to score, she makes everything she does look beautiful."

Nevertheless, fans were amused to see the whole Clark-Capobianco exchange, with some dubbing it "absolute comedy." Some even joked, saying that "caitlin gave bro his first smile of the night."

As Team USA fought to avoid its first loss at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in 20 years on Sunday, Clark had a rough night herself. She went scoreless from the field in her team's 55-52 win over Italy in Berlin. The Fever guard scored one point in the game and went 0-for-6 from the field. She also missed all three of her three-point attempts.

Clark played 19 minutes and recorded two turnovers, one steal, one assist, and four rebounds. Interestingly, the 24-year-old Team USA guard had never before gone an entire game without making a field goal at the WNBA or collegiate level. Her previous career low was three points on 1-of-10 shooting for Indiana against the New York Liberty in June 2024.

Together, Clark, Kahleah Cooper, and Breanna Stewart shot 1-for-19 from the field during the Sunday game. Overall, Stewart and Clark shot 1-for-15 from the field.

On Sunday, Team USA's remarkable winning streak was nearly over. With just 55 points against Italy, Team USA had its lowest scoring total since 1971.

Team USA hit 1-of-12 from three-point range and 29 percent from the field. Many believe Kara Lawson's team's 32-game winning streak could have ended if they hadn't had a significant lead in the charity stripe.

Per ESPN , speaking after the narrow win over Italy, Team USA head coach Lawson said, "We've seen that through the tournament that every game feels like a dogfight. It's really hard. On any given night, if you're not prepared to play, you'll lose."

The tight victory, in spite of the scare, guaranteed Team USA's place in the knockout round and increased the unprecedented World Cup winning streak to 32 games.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Updated Box Score Stats at FIBA World Cup After Making History with Rare Feat
articles.summary: After a brilliant start to the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, Caitlin Clark had a game to forget as the United States edged past Italy 55-52 on Sunday.
articles.body:
After a brilliant start to the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, Caitlin Clark had a game to forget as the United States edged past Italy 55-52 on Sunday.

Clark shot 0-of-6 from the floor, finishing with one point, four rebounds, one assist and one steal. That followed a record-setting performance in Team USA's opener.

Here's how the Indiana Fever guard's stats look like through two contests:

2 a.m. fire alarm disrupts FIBA teams at hotel

As the final score would indicate, Clark was far from the only U.S. player who struggled against the Italians. The United States' overall output was its lowest at the World Cup since 1971, and it shot 28.6 percent overall while having more turnovers (14) than assists (11).

For as much talent as Team USA has from top to bottom, A'ja Wilson's absence looms large. The score might've looked much different if the four-time WNBA MVP had been stationed in the paint.

The United States closes out the group phase Monday against Czechia, and it could be a great opportunity for Clark and others who lack a lot of international experience.

The Americans have already qualified for the quarterfinals by virtue of winning Group D. With little at stake, coach Kara Lawson may choose to rest her usual starters ahead of the knockout stage. In that case, Clark would be getting plenty of playing time.

articles.title: Japón - España en directo | Última hora de Mundial Femenino en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Ahora España tendrá dos días de descanso hasta el partido de cuartos de final. El rival saldrá del Australia contra el tercero del grupo D, a decidir
articles.body:
Última hora del Japón - España en directo:

¡¡¡Muuuuy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la última jornada de la fase de grupos del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto 2026 de Alemania !!! Último día de infarto para las cuatro selecciones que conforman este grupo A y que llegan empatadas (1-1) tras el batacazo de España ante Mali (82-73) el pasado sábado.

Las de Miguel Méndez afrontan esta primera final ante Japón con la obligación de ganar si no quiere sustos, aunque existe un escenario en el que una derrota también la clasificaría para octavos de final. España juega ante una selección nipona que sucumbió en la última jornada ante Alemania (74-58) , pero que venció a Mali (102-97) en una exhibición de triples . Un nuevo récord de 20 lanzamientos de tres de 35 intentos , con un tremendo 9/15 para Saki Hayashi .

España , a la que ya se le escapó el encuentro ante Mali por esa vía, deberá tener cuidado con uno de los puntos fuertes de las japonesas . Además, también deberá mejorar sus porcentajes en este aspecto. Pasó de un 14/28 (50%) en triples ante Alemania al 4/22 (18%) contra las africanas . El tiro libre también está siendo una piedra en la rueda de la Selección ; un 41% el primer día y un 53% el segundo.

Pese al lío formado entre los cuatro combinados, las cuentas son claras , donde las de Méndez tienen posibilidad de ocupar todas las posiciones. Si España gana hoy, será primera de grupo si Alemania hace lo propio con Mali ; en cambio, será segunda si las africanas también dan la sorpresa ante las anfitrionas . Los otros dos escenarios llegarían con la derrota de España ; si Mali gana a Alemania se salvaría y entraría como tercera , pero si las europeas vencieran a la verduga de la Selección serían cuartas y quedarían eliminadas.

Es decir, España tendrá que tener un ojo puesto en el otro partido que se juega de manera simultánea, ya que el resultado del Alemania-Mali influye directamente en la posición que ocupará. Si las de Méndez acaban primeras , jugarán directamente los cuartos el jueves 10 de septiembre . Pero si quedan segundas o terceras , tendrán menos descanso ya que jugarían una ronda más y disputarían los octavos de final en el día de mañana.

En definitiva, partido vital el que tiene la Selección esta tarde en Berlín . El Max Schmeling volverá a ser testigo de un nuevo encuentro de España , y nosotros, volveremos a contártelo con todo tipo de detalle. Esta tarde, desde las 17.50 horas , la Selección española se enfrenta a Japón para seguir con vida en este Mundial en el que hay tanta ilusión puesta, y lo viviremos como siempre, aquí, en MARCA .

Team USA has shot under 30 percent from three (20-of-69) across three games to open the World Cup, including just 21.6 percent (8-of-37) over the last two against Italy and Czechia.

Rhyne Howard is shooting 31.3 percent from deep, Caitlin Clark is at 25 percent and Napheesa Collier is at 20 percent.

articles.title: Thomas Walkup remata el colosal proyecto del Dubái Basketball
articles.standfirst: El equipo de los emiratos saca al base del Olympiacos, campeón de la Euroliga, con un contrato por tres temporadas y 9,6 millones de dólares
articles.summary: El equipo de los emiratos saca al base del Olympiacos, campeón de la Euroliga, con un contrato por tres temporadas y 9,6 millones de dólares
articles.body: El Dubái Basketball ha rematado su ambicioso segundo proyecto en la Euroliga con la incorporación de Thomas Walkup, base de 1,95 metros y 33 años que procede del Oympiacos, con el que se proclamó campeón de Europa la temporada pasada con promedios de 5,3 puntos, 2,6 rebotes, 5,7 asistencias y 0,9 robos. "Thomas es un fichaje muy importante para Dubai Basketball y otro paso adelante en la dirección que queremos tomar como club. Su conocimiento del juego, su competitividad y su capacidad para hacer mejores a los jugadores que le rodean serán extremadamente valiosos para nuestro equipo", valora Dejan Kamenjasevic, presidente de un Dubái Basketball que va con todo en busca de la Final Four. El equipo de los emiratos, que tendrá a Xavi Pascual en su banquillo, perseguía el fichaje del base desde hace tiempo y finalmente lo ha conseguido a golpe de talonario. Ha conseguido sacar al base de El Pireo pagando 2,6 millones de dólares y le ha puesto un contrato de 9,6 millones por tres campañas. Se hace así con uno de los bases más sólidos de la Euroliga en los últimos años y un defensor contrastado. La incorporación de Walkup se suma a las del exazulgrana Toko Shengelia, el exbaskonista Mamadi Diakite, Davion Mintz, Elie Okobo y Jaron Blossomgame. También estuvo cerca de contratar a Alpha Diallo, el mejor defensor de la Euroliga, aunque finalmente se marchó a los Nuggets. Todas esos fichajes se suman a las estrellas con las que ya contaba el conjunto emiratí: Dzanan Musa, McKinley Wright, Dwayne Bacon, Justin Anderson, Davis Bertans, Mfiondu Kabengele, Filip Petrusev... Hasta 18 jugadores tendrá Pascual a su disposición. Además, pensando en el futuro, el equipo de Dubái ha atado este verano a Kevin Kokila, que jugará en la Virtus Bolonia; a Yannick Kraag, que seguirá en el Asisa Joventut; Simonas Lukosius, que se irá al Unicaja; e incluso a Soumaila Keita, pívot maliense de 15 años y 2,12 metros que militaba en el Casademont Zaragoza.

articles.title: El camino de España en el Mundial: posibles cuartos ante Australia... y Estados Unidos en semifinales
articles.standfirst: La selección consigue el liderato del grupo, pero irá por el mismo lado del cuadro que las estadounidenses, favoritas al oro
articles.summary: La selección consigue el liderato del grupo, pero irá por el mismo lado del cuadro que las estadounidenses, favoritas al oro
articles.body: Después de las complicaciones que creó la sorprendente derrota ante Mali, la selección femenina consiguió el primer objetivo en el Mundial: el liderato del grupo. La victoria ante Japón (59-79) sumada al triunfo de Alemania (83-58) le dio la primera plaza. Eso le permite acceder directamente a cuartos de final sin necesidad de disputar un peligroso play-in de octavos. España no jugará ya hasta este jueves, cuando afronte esos cuartos de final. El rival saldrá del duelo entre Australia (C2) y el perdedor del Italia-China (D3) que cerrará la fase de grupos. Ese play-in se jugará este miércoles, con lo que el rival de la selección no tendrá descanso antes del cruce. Si el combinado de Miguel Méndez supera esos cuartos de final, se mediría en semifinales a Estados Unidos, que tiene garantizado el liderato de su grupo a falta del último partido. Pese al sufrido triunfo ante Italia, las estadounidenses siguen siendo las grandes favoritas al oro.

images.caption: Iyana Martín, durante el partido ante Japón. ALBERTO NEVADO/FEB

articles.title: España sufre, acaba líder y se mete en cuartos de forma directa
articles.standfirst: Gana a Japón en un partido con mucha tensión por lo que había en juego y en el que brilla Iyana Martín
articles.summary: Gana a Japón en un partido con mucha tensión por lo que había en juego y en el que brilla Iyana Martín
articles.body: España sacó adelante un complicadísimo partido ante Japón, 59-79, y con ello no solo se metió en la segunda fase, sino que lo hizo como líder de grupo y, por lo tanto, de forma directa para los cuartos de final del jueves, evitando el play-in de octavos. Pero tuvo que sufrir, y mucho. Es posible que Estados Unidos tenga a Caitlin Clark, pero España tiene una jugadora que va para superestrella y no tiene tanto que envidiarla. Iyana Martín iluminó el camino de la selección ante Japón, sobre todo en una primera parte a la que le sobraron los últimos dos minutos. Como ante Mali. Como se esperaba, Japón lo iba a fiar todo a su triple y a cortar el ritmo de España. En lo primero no estuvieron bien, 4/13 al descanso, 7/30 total. España incluso mejoraba eso, 4/11 y 8/25. Lo segundo se vio cuando en el primer cuarto ya sumaban 10 faltas y, a dos minutos para el final, las 12 jugadoras ya llevaban al menos una falta, eso sí, muy repartida. España, más entonada que ante Mali, llegó al final del primer cuarto con ventaja, 15-23, que quedó reducida por el 7-1 de Japón a la salida del segundo acto. Pero a 3:11 para el final, las de Méndez rompían el partido, 24-34, gracias a una canasta de mucho talento de Iyana. Y de nuevo la pájara de España. En apenas dos minutos la selección perdió su ventaja, 36-39 al descanso, con un parcial nipón de 12-5. Con las jugadoras en el vestuario, España sabía que solo le valía ganar el partido porque en el Uber Arena Alemania ganaba 49-32 a Mali. España salió más sólida en la reanudación y volvió a rondar los 10 de ventaja, 36-46 a 7:38 tras una canasta de Fam. Eran momentos en los que la selección era superior en el juego interior y, sobre todo, en la defensa, tratando de evitar los tiros cómodos de las japonesas. Las niponas, lejos de rendirse, intentaron volver al partido y lo hicieron con un par de triples para acercarse, 47-53 a 1:50, cuando Alemania ya ganaba por 22 a Mali. Una canasta de Carrera devolvió cierta tranquilidad a España, 48-57, cuando acababa el tercer episodio del partido. Japón jugaba sin la presión de la eliminación, porque la victoria alemana las clasificaba, como poco, en tercera posición. España, sin embargo, mostraba más tensión en sus gestos y en su juego. Pero las veteranas están para añadir tranquilidad y, tras dos fallos en el tiro libre, María Conde clavó un triple que devolvió los 10, 50-60, y a partir de ahí España ya controlaba el choque con la maravillosa Iyana a los mandos. Con Japón a la desesperada, España golpeó hasta una máxima de 15, 57-72, a dos minutos. Con el partido ganado, la selección aumentó esa máxima para un marcador que no resumió el enorme sufrimiento que pasó España para ganar y meterse directamente para los cuartos de final. Iyana no sólo guió con su juego a España hasta los cuartos, sino que fue la mejor anotadora, 20 puntos. Awa Fam hizo un doble-doble, 16+10 y Conde acabó con 9 puntos.

articles.title: Tigers' Jack Flaherty 'feeling good' after rehab appearance
articles.summary: The Tigers' Jack Flaherty threw 1⅓ scoreless innings for Triple-A Toledo, giving up a hit with a walk and two strikeouts at Fifth Third Field.
articles.body:
DETROIT — After throwing a bullpen session late last week, the logical next step for Tigers right-hander Jack Flaherty was to start his rehab assignment, getting him one step closer to returning the Tigers' rotation.

That next step took place Sunday evening, as Flaherty threw 1⅓ scoreless innings for Triple-A Toledo, giving up a hit with a walk and two strikeouts at Fifth Third Field.

"I think he came out feeling good and also a little critical of how his mechanics were and how he executed," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said Monday, Sept. 7, shortly before the Tigers hosted Minnesota in the first of three games at Comerica Park. "He had a walk in there and he ended up getting second (inning), which his nice.

"But I think the encouraging part is the recovery was good."

Flaherty has been out since July 21 with a flexor tendon strain and his been steadily working his way back.

On Sunday, he threw 19 pitches, allowing a one-out double in the first inning before issuing a two-out walk. He worked his way out of trouble with a strikeout to end the inning then returned for the top of the second, getting a groundout on the first pitch.

That was it, as Flaherty was pulled and now the Tigers plan the next step.

"He will do something in the next five days, or after five days," Hinch said, "kind of on the same cadence where he will throw a (bullpen session) and then we'll decide kind of what's next for him. (It could be) another outing or we can build some volume in a (simulated) game. We have a couple options, but we haven't finalized what the plan is.

"The first step was here today he felt great, and that's good."

Flaherty, who will be a free agent after the season, last pitched on July 20 against the Chicago Cubs. He is 3-8 this season with a 4.59 ERA in 19 starts over 86⅓ innings.

While the focus has shifted away from a realistic push for the playoffs over the final few weeks of the season, the Tigers are taking advantage of the opportunities offered some of their young, promising talent.

In Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Guardians , six rookies were in the starting lineup, and that's not necessarily a bad thing.

"That's a good step for those guys to get that type of experience and that type of challenge," Hinch said of facing Guardians starter Gavin Williams . "We've asked a lot of these guys to make pretty sizeable jumps when you look at young guys like ( John ) Peck , like ( Brett ) Callahan that are coming up pretty quickly.

"I'm encouraged by the fact guys are holding they're own. They're also seeing the challenge of the every day here. There are no easy days in the big leagues."

▶ First pitch: 6:40 p.m. Tuesday, Comerica Park, Detroit

▶ RHP Drew Anderson (4-5, 3.73), Tigers: This will be the second straight start Anderson makes against the Twins and right-hander Dean Kremer . In that start, Anderson left with the lead after going 5⅔ innings, giving up three hits and two runs (one earned) while striking out five.

▶ RHP Dean Kremer (2-5, 5.81), Twins: Kremer lasted only four innings in last week's start against the Tigers, allowing four runs and six hits as the Tigers went on to win, 11-6 in 12 innings. It was the second straight rough outing for Kremer, who gave up six runs in a loss to the White Sox on Aug. 28. This will be his fifth career start against Detroit and his third this season, the first coming while with the Baltimore Orioles.
authors: Matt Charboneau, Special to The Detroit News

articles.title: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter turns $427 NCAA suspension into powerful cancer research fundraiser
articles.summary: Arion Carter is donating $427 per tackle to Nashville cancer charities after his girlfriend Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer.
articles.body: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter walked out of the tunnel as the Vols’ sole captain during their home opener this past weekend, even though he was not suited up for the game. Amid the controversial decisions surrounding former professional athletes returning to college athletics, Carter accepted his punishment when he could have easily sought help from a local judge to create a path back onto the field. Following the 2025 season, the Vols linebacker decided to declare for the 2026 NFL Draft and leave Tennessee to pursue his professional dreams. TENNESSEE COACH UNLOADS ON NCAA'S 'BULLS–T', AFTER STAR LINEBACKER SUSPENDED FOR OUTDATED RULE Unfortunately, Carter found out he was dealing with a foot injury that would require him to have surgery and miss out on preparations for the upcoming draft. So, he made the decision to return to college. There were a few complications. Carter accepted $427 from an agent to cover a flight to a workout, and he knew his return to Tennessee could lead to an NCAA suspension. The NCAA's punishment came in the form of a one-game suspension that was initially set to keep the star linebacker out for the opening three games of the season. With all of the chaos surrounding college athletics — from state courtrooms to federal court — Carter handled the situation with the utmost respect. Carter is turning NCAA suspension into a fundraiser for cancer research Arion's girlfriend is currently in the middle of her own battle with cancer. To show his support, Carter recently shaved his head for the woman he loves. Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer earlier this year. She lives in the Nashville area, where she works as an ICU nurse at a local hospital. But now, he's also raising money for cancer research with his play on the field. First reported by Austin Price of VolQuest, Arion Carter will donate $427 for each tackle that he makes this season to Nashville area charities that support women struggling to pay bills during their battles with cancer. He is turning the $427 plane ticket reimbursement into something positive for the community, further demonstrating the character of a young man who has handled this entire ordeal with tremendous class. Wearing a "Team Jesus" shirt on Monday, Carter explained how he is turning a negative situation into a positive one. "It also goes back to my mom. She has always wanted a create a foundation, a non-profit for women and little girls," Carter reflected on Monday. "With my girlfriend, going what she's went though over these last few months, and me seeing it firsthand, it just really touched my heart and made me have a different perspective. "I wanted to raise awareness and set up a foundation for cancer research and be able to do this. So, that was the origin of that." The character of Arion Carter shines during this moment In addition to the first amount, Carter will donate $500 for each sack recorded this season, along with $1,000 for every interception or forced fumble. If he ends up scoring a touchdown while on defense, he will donate $5,000 for cancer research. COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY PRO ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT "I think it’s indicative of who he is, right? He’s passionate about a cause for multiple reasons – obviously for his girlfriend and his family history, as well," Tennessee's Josh Heupel said Monday. "He’s a guy that cares about community, so it’s indicative of who he is as a person." Although Carter repaid the $427 plane ticket, he was punished for declaring his intentions to enter the NFL Draft. While the rule may make sense on paper, the NCAA could have used this entire situation as a positive public-relations opportunity. "I feel like some things you can't control," Carter said. "I feel like you have to take everything with a grain of salt, not be too bitter about certain situations because there are rules at the end of the day. Even if the rules may not seem they are fair in a sense, I can’t control them. "This is another way for me to turn a negative into a positive and get the season started in a great way." Now, the Tennessee linebacker is writing his own story on how this all played-out, with the Vols set to battle Georgia Tech this weekend in Atlanta in primetime. articles.summary: Iyana Martin, primera jugadora menor de 21 años que anota al menos 20 puntos en dos partidos consecutivos de un Mundial
articles.body: Iyana Martín, mejor jugadora del partido en la victoria de España ante Japón (59-79), vive cada día "como si fuera el último, sin pensar en la edad" que tiene, dijo en rueda de prensa este lunes en Berlín tras otro gran partido y convertirse en la primera jugadora menor de 21 años que suma 20 puntos en dos partidos consecutivos. "Me centro en jugar al baloncesto. No tengo sabiduría de veterana. Me dejo llevar por el instinto. Todo consiste en seguir aprendiendo. El Mundial es una competición intensa, de mucho nivel, en la que los detalles importan", aseguró la líder de una España que ya está en cuartos de final del Mundial femenino. "Estoy en un equipo en el que puedo ser yo misma, pasarlo bien", añadió. Precisamente, su compañera de equipo Maite Cazorla dijo de la base ovetense que tiene "un desparpajo y una madurez que es de admirar". En zona mixta, también hablaron en el Max-Schmeling-Halle las jugadoras Maite Cazorla y Raquel Carrera. Ambas coincidieron en que a la selección le van a venir bien estas "48 horas para descansar y preparar el siguiente partido", en el que España se enfrentará al ganador del duelo de octavos de final entre Australia y, aún por decidir, Italia o China. Pero Carrera no tiene preferencia, ya que la selección ha demostrado que sabe adaptarse "a diferentes estilos de juego". "Hemos sabido sufrir y hemos sido persistentes. Sabíamos que eran un equipo de rachas, aunque metiesen 3 triples sabíamos que teníamos que seguir", dijo la base canaria tras la sufrida victoria ante el país nipón, que no refleja el resultado final lo ajustado que fue el partido.

articles.title: “She lost it and cried”: Stephen Curry opens up about the moment he saw his parents cry for him ahead of the new season
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors' star player, has been one of the finest athletes that the world has ever seen. While his talent has been inc.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors' star player, has been one of the finest athletes that the world has ever seen. While his talent has been incomparable, Stephen Curry has often reflected on how both his parents supported him and never forced him to take up a career in basketball even though his father, the Charlotte Hornets’ legend Dell Curry, is an NBA legend. Amid this, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry has opened up about when his family got emotional over him.Stephen Curry reflects on the moment his parents and especially his father, Dell Curry, got emotional over his talentIn an interview with Graham Bensinger, Stephen Curry opened up about the first round of the 2008 NCAA Tournament when the Davidson Wildcats defeated the Gonzaga Bulldogs.Back on March 21, 2008, Stephen Curry completely took over the game, scoring 40 points (including 30 in the second half) and hitting 8-of-10 from three-point range to lead 10th-seeded Davidson to an 82-76 comeback victory.The NBA legend reflected on the moment as he said, "I hit a three, I pointed at my mom and dad in the stands as I got back in on defense, and she lost it. Got really emotional, started crying.”Stephen Curry added, “My dad's showing the most emotion I've ever seen from him…He basically stood up, was yelling, and gave me a big fist bump in the air.”The four time NBA champion continued, “He usually just sits with his chin in his hands, no emotion, whether we're playing well, I have 40, or I have two points, he's always real stoic," he added. "That game, he just let loose, which is fun to see."Things changed in Stephen Curry’s life quickly as he was drafted by the Golden State Warriors in the first round as the 7th overall pick during the 2009 NBA Draft held at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey.After joining the Golden State Warriors, it did not take the NBA icon Stephen Curry too long to transform into one of the most legendary players that the world has ever seen.Stephen Curry reflects on being dedicated to the Golden State Warriors throughout his careerStephen Curry has also been committed to the Golden State Warriors throughout his career even as many rumors swirled about leading teams being interested in him.In a recent interview with NBC Sports Bay Area, Stephen Curry opened up about wanting to be in the Golden State Warriors as he said, "There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen…he deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity.”The NBA legend added, “Hopefully, we can be healthy and just have a chance to show what we're capable of, myself included, missing so many games last year."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Team USA offense revives in 105-64 win over Czechia at FIBA Women's World Cup to finish group play
articles.summary: Up next for Team USA in the tournament quarterfinals is the winner of Tuesday's Hungary-Japan matchup.
articles.body:
Team USA found its scoring touch for a 105-64 win over Czechia in its group play matchup at the FIBA Women's World Cup in Berlin on Monday.

The U.S. had already qualified for the quarterfinals of the tournament after winning its first two games in Group D competition. Meanwhile, Czechia was eliminated in the group stage after losing its first two games.

Breanna Stewart was hot from the start, notching 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting in the first quarter. She finished with 19 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists. Napheesa Collier, Jackie Young and Angel Reese each added 12 points. Collier also grabbed seven boards while Reese registered six in the win.

Every USA player scored at least one basket after Sonia Citron hit a baseline jumper at the end of the third. Citron finished with 10 points, as did Paige Bueckers. Caitlin Clark added 9 points and 7 assists, shooting 1-for-6 on 3-pointers.

The Americans only had one player score in double figures in Sunday's 55-52 win over Italy with Jackie Young tallying 10 points.

Team USA ended the first quarter with a 29-15 lead, shooting 52% from the floor. That was significantly encouraging after a 29% team shooting performance versus Italy.

The U.S. went ahead by 21 points with a 17-9 run through the first seven minutes of the second quarter and eventually took a 57-33 lead into halftime. That was more points than USA scored in Sunday's entire game.

The onslaught continued in the third quarter with Team USA opening up a 32-point margin after a 14-3 run.

Long-range shooting is still an issue for the Americans, who shot 28% (7 for 25) on 3-pointers. That was an improvement over the 1-for-12 (8%) effort versus Italy , but no USA player hit more than one shot from behind the arc against Czechia.

Eliska Joklova led Czechia with 19 points, hitting 11-of-14 free throws. She was the only Czechian player to reach double figures, though Julie Pospisilova scored nine while Natalie Stoupalova and Veronika Vorackova each got eight points.

Team USA has already qualified for the quarterfinals with three wins in Group D play. Those include a 94-61 win over China to open the tournament, along with the victory versus Italy. The Americans will face the winner of Tuesday's Hungary-Japan matchup on Thursday.

articles.title: “I have no idea who you are”: LeBron James opens up on never meeting his father and the impact it had on his life
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James, the NBA icon, has always been public about not having a father figure in his life as he was raised single handedly by his mother. This a.
articles.body: LeBron James, the NBA icon, has always been public about not having a father figure in his life as he was raised single handedly by his mother. This also had an influence on how he treats his three children as LeBron James has always been a present and a devoted father to them. Amid this, LeBron James has reflected on not ever meeting his father.LeBron James reflects on how not having a father in his life shaped his personality and the success he has achieved in his careerIn an interview with GQ, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player said, "Like, 'Wow, Dad, you know what, I don't know you, I have no idea who you are, but because of you is part of the reason who I am today.”The four time NBA champion added, ' The fuel that I use—you not being there—it's part of the reason I grew up to become who I am. It's part of the reason why I want to be hands-on with my endeavors. And be able to put my guys that's with me now in position. Like Maverick Carter, my right-hand guy in my business. Rich Paul, my agent. Randy Mims, my friend—he's my manager, you know.”The Philadelphia 76ers’ LeBron James continued, “So me in a position allowing people around me to grow, that maybe wouldn't have happened if I had two parents, two sisters, a dog, and a picket fence, you know?"In another post on his social media, the NBA icon wrote, “Because of you Pops! Thanks all along. Could have said why me with u not being there but look what I made of myself. Thanks to Huffington Post for the graphic. #StriveForGreatness”.LeBron James stepped up to be the father to his three children that he never had in his lifeLeBron James has always appreciated his mother for raising him and even being there for him when he and his now wife, Savannah James, found out they were expecting a child in 2004.The two were still in school and LeBron James had not even been drafted in the league yet.Not having a father in his life also prompted LeBron James to step up and fulfill his role as a parent when Savannah James found out she was pregnant.Coming from a pretty modest background in Akron, Ohio, things were incredibly difficult for LeBron James’ mother.However, she never gave up and fulfilled her role as a parent and today, LeBron James is easily one of the richest players in the world with billions of fans across continents.The NBA icon LeBron James is now gearing up for presumably his last season on the court as he eyes an NBA win this season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Francia es el coco
articles.standfirst: La selección gala ha arrollado en la primera fase, lidera las principales estadísticas y es la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos
articles.summary: La selección gala ha arrollado en la primera fase, lidera las principales estadísticas y es la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos
articles.body: Finalizada la primera fase, puede decirse que Francia es el coco del Mundial. Después de los tres primeros encuentros, la selección gala ha demostrado ser lo que se esperaba de ella antes del campeonato. Es un equipo mayúsculo. Tiene físico, calidad, amplitud, está trabajado, tiene estrellas... Y hambre. Antes de los cruces, cerró su grupo aplastando a Nigeria por 56-111 con récord de triples en un Mundial Femenino: 22/40. Si ya se consideraba a Francia como la gran candidata a acabar con el poder establecido de Estados Unidos (72-0 marcha desde 2006 en torneos a nivel planetario), el potencial que ha exhibido y las debilidades que han mostrado las norteamericanas reafirman esa sensación. Quizás puedan completar en Berlín la revolución que se quedaron a un paso de consumar en los Juegos de París, cuando perdieron la final por 67-66. Francia ha terminado como el mejor equipo de la fase de grupos dominando casi todas las estadísticas importantes. Ha sido líder en puntos (101,7), tiros de dos (66,7%), triples (48,5%), asistencias (26,7), recuperaciones (13,7) y valoración (132,7) y segunda en tiros libres (79,2%). Cifras aplastantes. "Este grupo, este equipo, está en otro nivel", asegura Gabby Williams, uno de los referentes ofensivos de la selección gala. La alero de 1,80 metros de las Golden State Valkyries es la máxima anotadora de lo que va de Mundial con 18,7 puntos de media y un sensacional 55% desde el triple. En valoración, está igualada con Emma Meesseman en lo alto de la estadística con 23,3 créditos, aunque ella juega 22,5 minutos por partido y la belga 31,2. Williams considera que "las francesas siempre han tenido mucho talento, pero la cultura ha cambiado. Ahora jugamos con intensidad. No importa lo talentosos que seamos. Si no lo das todo en la cancha, te van a sacar. No nos importa el marcador. No nos importa contra quién juguemos. Siempre tenemos que aportar la misma energía". Además, cree que "hay mucho talento en el banquillo". Tanto que nadie en la selección juega más de 24 minutos de media. También es un referente Marine Johannes, escolta de 1,78 que milita en las New York Liberty junto a Raquel Carrera. Es una fábrica andante de highlights. Las canastas imposibles son cosa suya. Hasta LeBron James alucinó con una serie de triples desequilibrados, en carrera o a una pierna que hizo hace tres años en un partido de WNBA. Es letal desde el arco: 52,0%. Y hasta ahora se está comportando con una regularidad propia de un reloj suizo: 17 puntos en cada uno de los tres encuentros que ha disputado. "Estamos contentas con cómo estamos jugando ahora mismo. Estamos compartiendo el balón, jugando una buena defensa para poder correr la cancha. Somos bastante buenas cuando movemos el balón rápidamente", dice Johannes. Las 26,7 asistencias que su equipo da por encuentro es una cifra escandalosa que muestra generosidad y capacidad para circular la pelota a tanta velocidad que los rivales se encuentran persiguiendo sombras. La tercera pata del sólido banco francés es Dominique Malonga, pívot de 1,97 que es compañera de Awa Fam en Seattle. Capaz de hacer mates, la jugadora nacida en senegal, es una fuerza de la naturaleza que se impone en la pintura. Nadie tiene mejor porcentaje que ella en tiros de dos puntos en este Mundial (73,7%). Hacerle llegar el balón bajo el aro es casi asegurar la canasta. Francia, como líder de su grupo, está ya en cuartos de final. Allí se medirá al ganador del duelo entre Puerto Rico y China. Favoritísima sea cual sea su rival. En semifinales, probablemente, se mediría a Bélgica. Es el camino hacia las medallas. La selección gala no consigue subir a un podio en un Mundial Femenino desde la primera edición, allá por 1953, cuando se colgó el bronce. Viendo su rendimiento, aspira a todo. Sí, incluso a acabar el trabajo que dejó a medias en París 2024.

articles.title: FSU-SMU game turns into old-school football after stadium power outage wipes out in-game communication
articles.summary: A power outage plunged Doak Campbell Stadium into darkness minutes before kickoff, forcing SMU and Florida State to play without communications.
articles.body: Just when we thought the college football weekend couldn’t get any crazier, a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium on the campus of Florida State sent school officials into a frenzy on Monday night in Tallahassee. Minutes before SMU and FSU were set to close out Labor Day weekend with there ACC game to finish week one, the lights went out inside the stadium that forced both teams back into the locker room. The game was scheduled to kickoff at 7:39 p.m. ET, but a power surge sent the stadium into darkness just as both teams had taking the field. Trust me, the jokes could write themselves for Florida State, but this unfortunate set of circumstances for everyone involved turned into a chaotic night. A very critical decision awaited, knowing there would also be no official replay during the game if both schools decided to play Both SMU and FSU decided to play the game without half the stadium having power . Every twenty minutes, officials from both schools and ACC commissioner Jim Phillips were meeting to discuss possible outcomes if they weren’t able to play the game on Monday night. For the fans, credit to them for sticking around through the madness, with games being played in the stands and the Florida State marching band trying their best to keep them all engaged. But, this was a mess. At 8:45 ET, following a third meeting between officials, the decision was made to play the game on Monday night without any type of communications. This included helmet-to-helmet comms, communication between coordinators or iPad usage along the sideline. Simply put, both teams decided to go full old-school tonight in Tallahassee. MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED The officials were having to practice hand signals with the coaches from both teams at 9:06 p.m. ET, while stadium officials were praying that the power would be fully-restored by the second half at the very least. No sideline communication for either team during the game I've seen some things covering this sport, but tonight is up their on the list on wildest events that have taken place in the past twenty years on the field. Both teams decided it would be a wise move to play without communications that are key for everyone involved in a college football game. And, sources told OutKick that there would have been an ample amount of problems for SMU to play this game on Tuesday. The Mustangs host UC Davis on Saturday, while the Seminoles have the weekend off. So, pushing this game back a day might have been the smart move, but would have been challenging for Rhett Lashlee and his football program. Also, you cannot just reschedule the game for later in the season for obvious reasons. The outcome was crucial for Florida State head coach Mike Norvell, who was already feeling the heat coming into the season. SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee noted that his team had not practiced without coach-to-player communication in over two years, so tonight was the first time since 2024 that he had not been in communication with his quarterback during a game. Even though both teams were dealing with the same problems Monday night, the result of this decision to play was going to haunt one of these coaches. In the end, this might have been fun for the fans inside Doak Campbell Stadium and those watching at home. articles.title: Kobe Bryant's wife Vanessa Bryant sends 4-word warm message to NFL power couple Ciara and Russell Wilson amid pregnancy news
articles.summary: NBA News: Kobe Bryant's wife Vanessa Bryant has sent a warm message to Ciara and Russell Wilson after the couple revealed they are expecting another child. Vane.
articles.body: Kobe Bryant's wife Vanessa Bryant has sent a warm message to Ciara and Russell Wilson after the couple revealed they are expecting another child. Vanessa shared her reaction on Instagram as the news spread among fans, offering a short but affectionate note to the growing family. Her message came shortly after Ciara and Wilson made their pregnancy announcement public on Sept. 6, giving followers a glimpse of the singer's baby bump and a playful reveal centered around their children.The announcement was filled with family touches, and the longtime friend of the couple, Vanessa's response added another personal moment to the celebration. Ciara and Wilson are already parents to three children together, while Ciara also has an older son from a previous relationship. Their latest addition will bring the household to seven, making the pregnancy another major chapter for the couple.Vanessa Bryant sends greetings to Ciara and Russell WilsonVanessa Bryant kept her reaction brief but affectionate. Sharing Ciara's pregnancy post on her Instagram story, she wrote, “Love you guys! Xo @ciara @dangerrusswilson.” Vanessa tagged both Ciara and Russell Wilson as she celebrated their happy news.Ciara, 40, and Wilson, 37, revealed the pregnancy on Instagram. Their post showed Ciara displaying her baby bump while standing beside a clothesline filled with children's shirts. Each shirt represented one of the couple's children, followed by a blank white baby onesie.Ciara captioned the announcement, “One more person to Love 🖐🏽🥺🖤.“Wilson joined the fun with a comment of his own: “Baby Cinco!”The pregnancy will be Ciara's fifth child and her fourth with Wilson. The couple already shares daughters Sienna Princess, 9, and Amora Princess, 2, along with son Win Harrison, 6. Ciara is also mom to Future Zahir, 12, whom she welcomed with rapper Future.Ciara's pregnancy announcement was built around familyRather than relying on a traditional pregnancy portrait, Ciara and Wilson made their children part of the reveal. The shirts bearing Future, Sienna, Win and Amora's names gave fans a clue before Ciara appeared with the baby onesie.In another part of the announcement, Ciara held up five fingers while showing off her bump. Wilson later walked along the clothesline before joining his wife, creating a playful reveal for the newest member of their family.The news also connects with comments Ciara has made about family life in recent years. After Amora's birth in December 2023, Ciara returned to music and toured while bringing her children along for parts of the journey.Speaking with PEOPLE in September 2024, she explained how important it was to have her children with her while she was on the road.“My kids traveled with me, and I couldn’t have done it any other way,” Ciara said.She also reflected on the quieter moments between performances. In an August 2024 Instagram post, Ciara described time with her children as the moments that “filled my cup” during tour life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “That’s always great to see”: Luka Doncic gets unwavering support from Former 2-time Slovenian Lakers champion
articles.summary: NBA News: Luka Doncic spent part of his offseason showing his new Los Angeles Lakers teammates where he grew up, hosting a minicamp in Slovenia after a roster s.
articles.body: Luka Doncic spent part of his offseason showing his new Los Angeles Lakers teammates where he grew up, hosting a minicamp in Slovenia after a roster shakeup that saw LeBron James depart. The trip mixed basketball, golf and downtime, all aimed at building chemistry before the 2026-27 season tips off.Fellow Slovenian Sasha Vujacic watched it thoroughly and came away impressed, while Lakers legend Robert Horry is not ready to hand out grades just yet. Their reactions frame a Lakers team still searching for its identity.Sasha Vujacic gives honest verdict on Luka DoncicLuka Doncic flew his new teammates out to Slovenia this summer, giving them a firsthand look at his home country before the grind of an NBA season sets in. Vujacic, who won two titles with the Lakers, sat down with ESPN Los Angeles and broke down what stood out most from the trip.Vujacic said the leadership has been obvious. He pointed to how Doncic opened up his home country to guys he had just started playing with, calling it a sign that his new teammate finally feels like a true Laker. "That's always great to see," Vujacic said.“It’s been there and what Luka has been doing, he’s showing the leadership. I’m very excited about this year. I think he’s finally a Laker, Laker. And him and AR and the team that we have, I can’t wait to watch it and for him to bring the team to Slovenia to show them where he comes from, to show everybody what Slovenia is all about,” Vujacic shared.“I think they have a better understanding of what it means for him to be in L.A. and through his journey how important it is to win.”Collin Sexton and Kevon Looney also came back from Slovenia with good things to say about their new teammate. Both players praised how welcoming Doncic had been, a detail that matters for a roster trying to gel fast after losing LeBron James.Former Lakers star Robert Horry has a different opinion on Luka DoncicThe Lakers enter the season with a roster that looks almost nothing like last year's group. LeBron James is gone, and the front office brought in Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Kevon Looney, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Matisse Thybulle and Zaire Williams over the summer.Horry, who won seven championships across his career, is not rushing to judge how it all fits together. He wants to see the pieces play real minutes before forming an opinion. "I'm going to hold back right now because I want to see them," Horry said on ESPN LA.He described the new additions as specialists, players who excel in specific roles but will need time adjusting to coach JJ Redick's system. Kessler, at 7-foot-2, is expected to anchor the frontcourt and protect the rim, while Grimes and Sexton add scoring depth off the bench.Doncic and Austin Reaves anchored the offense a season ago, with Doncic putting up a league-high 33.5 points a game. The new faces around them will decide how quickly the Lakers close the gap between talent and chemistry. Thybulle, Grimes and Williams give the Lakers more length on the wing, joining Jarred Vanderbilt as options to shore up a defense that will look different from a year ago.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aari McDonald signs with Minnesota Lynx
articles.summary: It’s been a long time since former Arizona star Aari McDonald played in a WNBA game. That has come to an end with the first-place Minnesota Lynx announcing h...
articles.body:
It's been a long time since former Arizona star Aari McDonald played in a WNBA game. That has come to an end with the first-place Minnesota Lynx announcing her signing on Monday afternoon.

McDonald was injured last August while playing for the Indiana Fever. She tried to come back by playing in the Unrivaled 3×3 league during the WNBA offseason, but she was again sidelined by injury. As WNBA training camp approached this year, she said she would not be in camp but she would return this season. It took a while, but now she's not only returning, but she's doing it with the best team in the league.

The Lynx lead the WNBA standings with a 31-9 record and four games left in the regular season. The league returns to play on Sept. 18 after a break for the FIBA Women's World Cup where many top players are representing their countries. That event runs from Sept. 4-13, but the league shut down on Aug. 31.

McDonald sat out a large chunk of last season after being waived by the LA Sparks in training camp. She eventually landed with the Indiana Fever, where she quickly became a fan favorite of the passionate fan base and a fixture in the local community.

She averaged 9.8 points on 42.9 percent shooting, 4.7 assists, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.3 steals in 26.3 minutes per game for Indiana last season. She appeared in 20 games with 13 starts. It was a career high in games started, minutes per game, field goal percentage, assists per game, and rebounds per game.

Over the course of her career, she has averaged 8.8 points on 39.5 percent shooting, 3.1 assists, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals in 22.3 minutes per game. She has made 136 appearances and 42 starts for three different teams.

McDonald was drafted third in the 2021 draft by the Atlanta Dream just weeks after leading Arizona to its first and only national championship appearance. The Wildcats fell to Stanford by one point after dismissing UConn in the national semifinal.

During her time with Arizona, she won the 2020 Ann Meyers Drysdale award, the 2020 and 2021 Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year award, and the 2021 Pac-12 Player of the Year award. She joined Arizona's Ring of Honor the year after she turned pro.

Her time with the Minnesota will be her third time being on a playoff team, although she was injured when Indiana made last year's playoffs. She made two playoff appearances with the Atlanta Dream in 2023.

McDonald was also recently announced as an addition to Melikgazi Kayseri Basketbol in the Turkish KBSL for the 2026-27 season. The team will be looking to make a turnaround this year after finishing 6-14 in the KBSL last year. They fell to Fenerbahçe in the quarterfinals of the league playoffs. The organization had its best run during the early-to-mid 2010s when it was a quarterfinalist in EuroLeague (2013-14), the EuroCup runners-up three times, and the runner-up in the KBSL (2014-15).

McDonald's last season overseas was spent in China during the 2024-25 season. She spent the season before that in Australia where she was the league scoring champion with 19.8 ppg and helped her team reach the WNBL Grand Final. Her team, the Perth Lynx, finished as the WNBL runner-up.
